correctness.rationale: In fixed standard successor arithmetic every allowed equality is an atom E_j or a Boolean constant after cancellation. A knowing-value target is either rigid or an injective successor shift of c. Work inside the root's equivalence class: by induction a formula has the same truth at all worlds of a given tag for fixed class signature. In the K step the class is unchanged at each world, and only the set of present tags matters. In the Kv step each selected named tag supplies one value; if selected, the outside tag supplies 0, 1 or at least 2 values, and the only test is whether the total is at most one. This applies to arbitrary finite formula nesting even on infinite classes. Conversely, root tags are tested by atoms; possibility of each E_j gives the named support; possibility of E_* and Kv(E_*,c) distinguish all three outside cases, including vacuity. Consequently each realized signature and every union of signatures are definable at depth one. An all-unnamed one-value point and a two-value point give depth-zero equivalence but different Kv truth, also at k=0. One representative per named value and r distinct unnamed representatives are both necessary and sufficient, with maximum k+2. For r=0 each nonempty T contributes |T| root choices; for each of r=1,2 each T contributes |T|+1. Summing yields 3k*2^(k-1)+2^(k+1) for k>=1 and two theories at k=0. All subsets of these theories being definable gives exactly 2^N_k formula classes.
residual_risks: Finite refinement is a bounded check. It does not cover arbitrarily large supports or k; induction and characteristic formulas prove the unrestricted claim under the stated one-agent standard semantics.
